SYNTHESIZED — no real OpenCode store was available on this machine.

This fixture mimics the native shape of the OpenCode SQLite session store
`<data_dir>/opencode.db` as executed by the golden test with `rusqlite`
(no committed binaries): a `session` table (one row per native session:
`id`, `cwd`, `version`, `created_at`) plus a `message` table (one row per
record: `id` rowid cursor key, `session_id`, `role`, `name`, `content`,
`reasoning`, token counters, `is_error`, `ts`). Roles follow the brief's
mapping contract — `user` records carry prompt text; `assistant` records
carry model, text, optional reasoning, and token usage; `tool_call` rows
carry the tool name with a JSON-encoded input object in `content`
(`Edit`/`Write` inputs with `file_path` additionally yield `file_change`
plus `files_touched`); `tool_result` rows carry the output text;
`summary` rows carry compaction context. The assistant row's inline
`reasoning` and the `Edit` row's file-write part each emit two events, so
the fixture exercises the multi-event resume path. Session id, version,
token counts, and prose are invented. It is not a captured production
database.
